newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds inch lower on overseas profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds inch lower on overseas profit taking.

text.p: Irish government bonds took a breather in patchy trade on Wednesday as the recent buoyancy in the market eased as overseas buyers took time out to consider their options, dealers said.
"Buyers have been in and out all day but there has also been a little opportunistic profit taking. Most levels are still very healthy," one dealer said.
By 1522 GMT the eight percent bond due 2001 was down 17p at 104.66 to yield 6.40 while the eight percent bond due 2006 was down 31 pence at 105.09 to yield 7.14.

"A lot of positive factors in recent days have helped the Irish bond market. Renewed Irish confidence in EMU, the Irish pound's ERM performance, overseas bidding appetite and a strong dollar/mark level are all very much in Ireland's favour," one dealer said.
Dealers echoed the belief in the market that next week's FOMC monetary meeting would announce a 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates.
Earlier, UK retail sales data for August hit the gilt market when it came in higher than expected. Sales grew at 4.4 percent year-on-year against forecasts of 3.5 percent.
Gilts recovered a little later when U.S. international trade data showed the widest deficit since the fourth quarter of 1987.
Market observers said the figures could contribute to a mildly better tone in the short term.
Dublin dealers said they would be focusing on Thursday's Irish balance of international payments data for the first quarter of 1996.
